name: PayPal

header.value: PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-ID, PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-TIME, PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-SIG, PAYPAL-CERT-URL and PAYPAL-AUTH-ALGO
header.quote: The unique ID of the transmission, from the paypal-transmission-id

header_auth_algo_and_cert_url.value: PAYPAL-AUTH-ALGO carries the algorithm (example value SHA256withRSA); PAYPAL-CERT-URL carries the certificate URL
header_auth_algo_and_cert_url.quote: Extract this value from the `PAYPAL-AUTH-ALGO` response header, which is received with the webhook notification.

scheme.value: Asymmetric: RSA signature, SHA256withRSA, verified with the public key from the X.509 certificate at PAYPAL-CERT-URL. The signature header value is base64 (the sample listener decodes it with Buffer.from(sig, 'base64') and verifies with SHA256). No shared secret.
scheme.quote: Use it to validate the signature given by the header paypal-transmission-sig
scheme.short: RSA with SHA-256 (SHA256withRSA), checked with PayPal's certificate; no shared secret

signed_content.value: the string transmissionId|timeStamp|webhookId|crc32 (four fields joined by the pipe character; the guide shows a trailing semicolon after the template). transmissionId = PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-ID header; timeStamp = PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-TIME header; webhookId = the ID of the subscribed webhook from the dashboard (not in headers or body); crc32 = CRC32 of the raw body as a decimal integer.
signed_content.short: {transmission id}|{transmission time}|{webhook id}|{CRC32 of the raw body, decimal}

crc32_detail.value: CRC32 of the raw HTTP body in decimal form; do not parse and re-stringify. The sample listener computes it as parseInt('0x' + crc32(rawBody).toString('hex')).
crc32_detail.quote: The Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC32) checksum for the body of the HTTP payload, in decimal form. You must use the original raw body to calculate this

header_format.value: five separate headers (not one combined header); no multiple-signature list described

secret_source.value: No secret. The webhook ID (needed to rebuild the signed string and for the verify API) is shown when the listener URL is subscribed, in Application management under the app's settings, or returned by the Webhooks Management API. The certificate is downloaded from PAYPAL-CERT-URL and may be cached.
secret_source.quote: When you subscribe a listener URL, it will have a Webhook ID. Record the ID as it is needed for verification of all webhook messages sent to that URL.
secret_source.short: No secret: the webhook ID from the app's settings, and the certificate at PAYPAL-CERT-URL

secret_scope.value: webhook ID is per subscribed listener URL (up to 10 URLs per app); events are per app
secret_scope.quote: Up to 10 webhook URLs may be subscribed per app.

cert_host_restriction.value: not stated by the provider. The guide's sample listener downloads whatever URL arrives in PAYPAL-CERT-URL without checking its host; the guide does not say which hosts a legitimate certificate comes from. (Example cert URL seen: https://api.sandbox.paypal.com/v1/notifications/certs/CERT-...)

rotation.value: not stated by the provider (certificate is downloaded from the header URL and cached; no rotation behaviour described)
rotation.quote: This file should automatically be downloaded and cached for future use.

raw_body_note.value: Use the original raw body for the CRC32; for the postback method, post webhook_event back byte-identical with no re-serialization.
raw_body_note.quote: It is essential that the webhook_event data be posted back exactly as it was received, with no deviations in formatting or content of any kind.

verify_api.value: POST /v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature (Bearer access token, JSON body). Required request fields: auth_algo (from PAYPAL-AUTH-ALGO), cert_url (PAYPAL-CERT-URL), transmission_id (PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-ID, max 50), transmission_sig (PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-SIG), transmission_time (PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-TIME, RFC 3339), webhook_id (from the developer portal, max 50), webhook_event (the event body). Response: {verification_status: SUCCESS | FAILURE}. Hosts shown: api.sandbox.paypal.com for sandbox, api-m.paypal.com for live. Not usable for simulator mock events.
verify_api.quote: The status of the signature verification.

verify_api_guide_quote.value: the guide's curl example for the postback method

preferred_method.value: PayPal says self verification (CRC32 + certificate) is preferred when the system can do it, as it is faster and avoids an extra API dependency; postback is the alternative.
preferred_method.quote: self cryptographic verification is the preferred method as it will be faster and avoid extra API dependency and latency.

node.value: not stated by the provider (the guide gives a hand-written Express sample using crypto.createVerify('SHA256') and buffer-crc32, not an SDK helper)

mock_event_webhook_id.value: For simulator (mock) events, self verification uses the literal webhook ID string WEBHOOK_ID
mock_event_webhook_id.quote: For message signature verification purposes, the ID of mock webhooks is the string: WEBHOOK_ID

method_and_content_type.value: HTTPS POST to a listener on port 443 only. Content-Type not stated in words; the guide's sample listener reads the body with express.raw({type: 'application/json'}) and JSON.parse.
method_and_content_type.quote: Webhooks are HTTPS posts from PayPal to an endpoint on your server whenever the corresponding event type occurs

event_type_location.value: body JSON field event_type (for example PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED); also resource_type, event_version, resource_version, summary, resource, links, create_time
event_type_location.quote: The event that triggered the webhook event notification.

delivery_id.value: event id: body field id (for example WH-3F562076HD293871E-75F399086E414290U); the transmission id header differs per transmission attempt per PayPal's description 'ID of the HTTP transmission'. PayPal's pages do not explicitly tell receivers which to dedupe on.
delivery_id.quote: The ID of the webhook event notification.

resource_version.value: body field resource_version (string, example 2.0) versions the shape of the resource object; event_version (example 1.0) is marked deprecated in the spec. The guide does not describe resource_version in prose.

batching.value: one event per message; each message is posted to every subscribed listener URL
batching.quote: Messages for events will be posted to every subscribed listener URL.

success_status.value: HTTP 200 or any other 2xx; any non-2xx triggers retry
success_status.quote: Successful receipt requires your listener endpoint to respond with an HTTP 200 or other 2xx status code.

retries.value: up to 25 attempts over 3 days, or until a 2xx arrives; per-attempt schedule not given. After 3 days the delivery is marked Failed and can be resent manually from the Webhook Events dashboard (or via the resend event notification API).
retries.quote: Any non-2xx status code will cause PayPal to reattempt delivery up to 25 times over the course of 3 days or until it receives a 2xx success code.

disabling.quote: If unsuccessful after 3 days, delivery will be marked as Failed (but can be resent again manually from the Webhook Events dashboard).

duplicates.value: not stated by the provider (retries and manual resends exist, so duplicates are possible, but PayPal's pages do not say so)
duplicates.quote: PayPal will retry each delivery up to 25 times over 3 days.

common.meaning: a payment capture was denied (listed under Payments v1)
a payment capture was declined (listed under Payments v2); both DENIED and DECLINED appear in the docs

common.quote: A merchant refunds a payment capture.

common.meaning: buyer approved an order; ready to capture
common.quote: A buyer approved a checkout order

common.meaning: a sale completed (for example each subscription cycle payment)
a dispute was opened; supersedes and deprecates RISK.DISPUTE.CREATED

where_url_is_entered.value: Application management (developer dashboard), under each app's settings, or the Webhooks Management API. Up to 10 URLs per app; subscribe specific event types or * for all. Listener must be HTTPS on port 443.
where_url_is_entered.quote: Your listener should be an app or script deployed at the corresponding URL that listens on HTTPS port 443.

test_tools.value: Webhooks simulator (post a mock event to any listener on HTTPS 443; also POST /v1/notifications/simulate-event). Mock events: not tied to an app, not in the dashboard event viewer, cannot be resent, cannot be verified with the verify-webhook-signature postback, self-verify with webhook ID WEBHOOK_ID. Sandbox: subscribe the listener to a sandbox REST app and generate real test events. Real events can be resent from the Webhook Events dashboard.
test_tools.quote: They cannot be verified by posting back to the PayPal verify-webhook-signature endpoint

gotchas.value: PayPal only delivers to HTTPS port 443.
gotchas.quote: PayPal only delivers webhooks to port 443 (HTTPS).

gotchas.value: If you do not verify, nothing proves the sender is PayPal.
gotchas.quote: If you do not verify a message, you will not have a way to validate that its sender was in fact PayPal.

gotchas.value: The webhook ID is not in the headers or body; you must store it from the subscription config.
gotchas.quote: This does not come in the header or body of the message but rather where the webhook listener URL's event subscriptions are configured

gotchas.value: Delivery can fail with no HTTP status at all if a firewall blocks port 443 or the domain is categorised as malware or abusive by URL filtering services.
gotchas.quote: if the domain webhooks are being sent to is marked as malware, phishing, or as involved in some other abuse by url filtering services.

gotchas.value: Events only arrive for the specific app the URL is subscribed on; the legacy NVP/SOAP app is separate and excludes NVP/SOAP recurring payments.
gotchas.quote: Only events associated with the specific app will be received

unreadable.why: client-rendered shell; only endpoint titles visible; request fields taken from PayPal's own OpenAPI spec repo instead

research_notes: Event names page lists PAYMENT.CAPTURE.DENIED under Payments v1 and PAYMENT.CAPTURE.DECLINED under Payments v2; both exist in the docs.
BILLING.SUBSCRIPTION.CANCELLED is listed twice, as 'A billing agreement is canceled' (legacy billing plans and agreements) and as 'A subscription is cancelled' (Subscriptions).
